question.text: In a UNIFIED fund structure, commitments from both domestic and offshore investors are:

answer.text: Pooled into two separate vehicles — one onshore and one offshore — which invest independently
Pooled into a single domestic (onshore) AIF registered in India, with offshore investors investing via FPI/FDI route
Collected by the manager and placed in personal brokerage accounts
Split by nationality with offshore investors bypassing SEBI registration entirely

explanation.text: The Logic: In a Unified Structure, commitments from both domestic and foreign investors are pooled into ONE onshore AIF in India, with offshore investors routing in under the FPI or FDI route. The workbook also describes a related arrangement where an offshore fund itself invests into the onshore AIF. The Trap: Option A describes a Parallel Structure (two vehicles). Option C is fabricated. Option D is wrong — SEBI/FEMA compliance is still required. Note: The workbook (pp. 127-128, 131) describes unified-structure mechanics and the offshore-fund-to-onshore-AIF arrangement, but does not provide the specific tax-planning advice in the original pro-tip.
